facts.statement: Callovosaurus is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur known primarily from a nearly complete left thigh bone found in Middle Jurassic rocks in England.
facts.quote: Callovosaurus (meaning "Callovian lizard") is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur known from most of a left thigh bone discovered in Middle Jurassic-age rocks of England.

facts.statement: The type specimen's thigh bone is 28 cm long, suggesting the animal was approximately 2.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: The bone is 28 cm long, and is estimated to have belonged to an animal approximately 2.5 m in length.

facts.statement: The fossil was collected from the Peterborough Member of the Oxford Clay Formation near Peterborough in Cambridgeshire, England.
facts.quote: This specimen was collected from the middle Callovian–age (Middle Jurassic) Peterborough Member (former Lower Oxford Clay) of the Oxford Clay Formation of Fletton, near Peterborough in Cambridgeshire, England.

facts.statement: The species was first described by Richard Lydekker in 1889 under the name Camptosaurus leedsi.
facts.quote: The type species, C. leedsi, was first described by Richard Lydekker in 1889 as Camptosaurus leedsi

facts.statement: Peter Galton established the new genus Callovosaurus for the species in 1980.
facts.quote: he then gave the species the new genus Callovosaurus in 1980

facts.statement: The validity of Callovosaurus has been debated, with some researchers considering it a dubious genus or a basal dryosaurid.
facts.quote: At times, it has been considered dubious or a valid genus of basal iguanodontian, perhaps a dryosaurid.

facts.statement: A 2025 study found Callovosaurus to be more basal than previously thought and placed it outside the families Dryosauridae and Dryomorpha.
facts.quote: Though a study published in 2025 from Łukasz Czepiński & Daniel Madzia found Callovosaurus to be more basal than once thought and found Callovosaurus outside of the family Dryosauridae and Dryomorpha as a whole.

facts.statement: Callovosaurus lived alongside diverse reptiles including ichthyosaurs, plesiosaurs, crocodyliforms, pterosaurs, sauropods, stegosaurids, and the armored dinosaur Sarcolestes.
facts.quote: Callovosaurus was found in the lower Oxford Clay, which has yielded a diverse reptile assemblage: ichthyosaurs, plesiosaurs, crocodyliforms, pterosaurs, sauropod dinosaurs, the stegosaurids Loricatosaurus and Lexovisaurus, and the armoured dinosaur Sarcolestes.

facts.statement: Callovosaurus was a herbivore, feeding on plant material like other iguanodontians.
facts.quote: The diet of Callovosaurus, like that of other iguanodontians, was plant material.

facts.statement: It is probable that Callovosaurus traveled in herds to protect itself from predators, a behavior inferred from better-known ornithopods like Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Es probable que el Callovosaurus viajara en manadas, un comportamiento basado en ornitópodos mejor conocidos como el Iguanodon, para protegerse y evitar ser atacado por estos depredadores.

facts.statement: Callovosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 162 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 162 millones de años, en la etapa Calloviense, en lo hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The time range for Callovosaurus is estimated to be between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Researchers have proposed that Callovosaurus is a valid genus and potentially the oldest known dryosaurid.
rejected.quote: Jose Ignacio Ruiz-Omeñaca and coauthors have proposed that Callovosaurus is a valid genus, and the oldest known dryosaurid.
